title: How would you explain earth to aliens?
description:
The Voyager 1 space probe reached the milestone of travelling one light day away from Earth this week. That’s the furthest any manmade object has ever travelled. It’s one of two spacecrafts NASA launched in 1977 hoping to explore the outer reaches of our solar system.

Just in case aliens intercept either of the space probes, NASA placed identical gold-plated records on each of them carrying a message from planet Earth. The NASA team chose dozens of sounds, songs and pictures to represent our planet.

BBC journalist Kaine Pier explains what’s on the records and how NASA’s team decided what to put on them. We also hear from Ann Druyan, creative director of the golden record project, and Jon Lomberg, its design director.

summaryEn: This episode of What in the World explores NASA's Golden Record carried by the Voyager space probes. BBC journalist Caine Pieri joins host Hannah Gelbart to explain how creative director Ann Druyan and design director Jon Lomberg curated a diverse selection of global music, natural sounds, photos, and brainwaves on a gold-plated copper disc designed to last billions of years. The team deliberately excluded negative aspects of humanity such as war and famine, creating a hopeful time capsule and bottle message for potential extraterrestrial life.

So all of these rather amazing images trying to sum up humanity in one record, but nothing to do with conflict, crime, famine, genocide, or any of the things that plague humanity.
There was, it was quite a, it was a nihilistic picture in a way.

It was simply intended as a message to try to answer the questions that we think anybody who finds this message would have, which we think would be the same message, the same questions that we would have if we were to find an artifact: Who made it? What were they like? What did they look like? What was their biochemistry like? What was their planet like?
